questions.explain: Vue slide: **progressive framework for UIs**, Evan You, 2014, MIT license, vuejs.org.

questions.prompt: In the Composition API, what is `setup()`?
options: The entry point that declares reactive state and returns what the template can use
A lifecycle hook that runs on unmount
A method for registering global components
The function that mounts the app
questions.explain: setup() = Composition API **entry point**; whatever it returns is template-visible — nothing else is.

questions.prompt: Given `const count = ref(0)`, how do you increment it in a JS function and render it in the template?
options: count.value++ in script / {{ count }} in template
questions.explain: **`.value` in script, auto-unwrapped in template** — the #1 Vue trap. `{{ count.value }}` in a template is wrong (renders undefined-ish for nested cases); `count++` in script doesn't touch the inner value.

questions.prompt: Which directive shorthand pair is correct?
options: v-bind shorthand is ':', v-on shorthand is '@'
v-bind shorthand is '@', v-on shorthand is ':'

questions.prompt: v-if vs v-show — which is TRUE?
options: v-if adds/removes the element from the DOM; v-show keeps it rendered and toggles CSS display
v-show removes the element from the DOM
questions.explain: v-if = DOM add/remove (rare toggles); v-show = display toggle (frequent toggles).

questions.prompt: A computed property differs from a method because it:
options: Is cached and re-evaluates only when its dependencies change
questions.explain: Computed = **cached + dependency-tracked**; methods re-run every call.

questions.prompt: After all `app.use(...)` calls, which method attaches the Vue app to `#app`? (method name only)
questions.explain: `app.mount('#app')` — always the LAST call in main.js / the CDN bootstrap.

questions.prompt: `const user = reactive({ age: 22 })` vs `const user2 = ref({ age: 22 })` — how do you increment each age in script?
questions.explain: **reactive** objects mutate via plain property access (no .value); a **ref holding an object** goes through `.value` first. That asymmetry is a favourite exam trap.
